docs.title: CV Pipeline Inspector
docs.text: Computer vision defect detection on pipeline inspection imagery using image analysis.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "CV Pipeline Inspector", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Data Generator: Creates synthetic pipeline defect samples with 14 image features
  • Defect Types: corrosion, cracks, dents, leaks, weld_defects, healthy
  • Training Data: 300 samples per class, 80/20 train/test split
  • Feature Vector: 14-dimensional (pixel stats, edge, texture, color, gradients)

docs.title: Defect Classifier (DefectClassifier)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Ensemble of RandomForest + GradientBoosting
  • RandomForest: 100 estimators, max_depth=15, min_samples_split=5
  • GradientBoosting: 100 estimators, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.1
  • Voting: Soft voting (average predicted probabilities)
  • Evaluation: Cross-validation accuracy + test set accuracy
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Severity Estimator (SeverityEstimator)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoosting Regressor
  • Parameters: 100 estimators, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.1
  • Output: Continuous score 0-10
  • Levels: low (<3), medium (3-6), high (6-8), critical (>8)
  • Evaluation: MAE, R2 score, cross-validation R2
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Anomaly Detector (DefectDetector)
docs.text:
• Algorithm: Isolation Forest (unsupervised)
  • Parameters: contamination=0.15, 100 estimators
  • Input: Normal data only (unsupervised training)
  • Output: Binary label (normal/anomaly) + anomaly score
  • Persistence: Pickle (.pkl)

docs.title: Image Feature Extractor (ImageFeatureExtractor)
docs.text:
• Approach: Simulated feature extraction from synthetic image data
  • Features: 14 handcrafted features (intensity, edge, texture, color, gradient)

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask (Python)
  • Serialization: JSON request/response
  • Model Loading: Pickle deserialization at startup
  • Port: 5016

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (single page)
  • Visualization: Chart.js for metrics and results
  • Style: Dark-themed responsive UI

docs.title: Classification Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Input Feature Vector (14 dimensions)
   ↓
2. DefectClassifier
   ├── RandomForest Prediction
   └── GradientBoosting Prediction
   ↓
3. Soft Voting (Probability Averaging)
   ↓
4. Defect Type + Confidence
   ↓
5. Dashboard Display

docs.title: Severity Estimation Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Input Feature Vector (14 dimensions)
   ↓
2. SeverityEstimator (GradientBoosting)
   ↓
3. Continuous Score (0-10)
   ↓
4. Severity Level Mapping
   ↓
5. Score + Level Output

docs.title: Anomaly Detection Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Input Feature Vector(s)
   ↓
2. Isolation Forest
   ↓
3. Binary Prediction (-1=anomaly, 1=normal)
   ↓
4. Anomaly Score (lower = more anomalous)
   ↓
5. Label + Score Output

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn with multiple workers for production deployments
  • Ensure debug=False in app.py (already set by default)
  • Configure proper logging for request/error tracking
  • Place behind a reverse proxy (nginx/Apache) for SSL termination
  • Models load from outputs/models/ - ensure this directory exists
  • Pre-train models with train.py before starting the server

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: CV Pipeline Inspector is a machine learning system for detecting, classifying, and estimating the severity of defects in pipeline infrastructure. It analyzes 14 image features per sample using ensemble models.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd cv-pipeline-inspector
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

Generates synthetic training data and trains all three models (classifier, severity estimator, anomaly detector). Models are saved to outputs/models/.

docs.title: Start the API Server
docs.text:
python app.py

The server starts on http://localhost:5016.

docs.title: Open the Dashboard
docs.text: Navigate to http://localhost:5016 in your browser.

docs.title: Run Tests
docs.text: python test_api.py

docs.title: Dashboard Features
docs.text:
• Defect Classification: Upload feature vectors to classify defect types
  • Severity Estimation: Get severity scores (0-10 scale) with severity levels
  • Anomaly Detection: Run unsupervised anomaly detection on feature data
  • Model Statistics: View training metrics for all models

docs.title: Defect Types
docs.text: Type Description corrosion Surface degradation and rust formation cracks Structural fractures in pipeline material dents Physical deformations from impact leaks Fluid escape points in pipeline weld_defects Imperfections in welded joints healthy No defects detected

docs.title: Using curl
docs.text:
Classify a defect:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5016/api/classify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"features": [120.5, 30.2, 0.25, 4.1, 140.0, 120.0, 100.0, 0.55, 1200.0, 30.0, 120.0, 0.1, 18.0, 0.25]}'

Estimate severity:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5016/api/severity \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"features": [120.5, 30.2, 0.25, 4.1, 140.0, 120.0, 100.0, 0.55, 1200.0, 30.0, 120.0, 0.1, 18.0, 0.25]}'

Detect anomalies:

curl -X POST http://localhost:5016/api/detect \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"features": [120.5, 30.2, 0.25, 4.1, 140.0, 120.0, 100.0, 0.55, 1200.0, 30.0, 120.0, 0.1, 18.0, 0.25]}'

docs.title: Using Python
docs.text:
import requests

features = [120.5, 30.2, 0.25, 4.1, 140.0, 120.0, 100.0, 0.55, 1200.0, 30.0, 120.0, 0.1, 18.0, 0.25]

# Classify defect type
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5016/api/classify", json={"features": features})
result = response.json()
print(f"Defect: {result['classifications'][0]['defect_type']}")
print(f"Confidence: {result['classifications'][0]['confidence']:.2%}")

# Estimate severity
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5016/api/severity", json={"features": features})
result = response.json()
sev = result['severity'][0]
print(f"Severity: {sev['severity_score']:.1f}/10 ({sev['severity_level']})")

# Detect anomalies
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5016/api/detect", json={"features": features})
result = response.json()
det = result['detections'][0]
print(f"Anomaly: {det['label']} (score: {det['anomaly_score']:.4f})")

docs.title: Batch Processing
docs.text:
import requests
import numpy as np

# Generate multiple feature vectors
batch_features = np.random.rand(10, 14).tolist()

response = requests.post("http://localhost:5016/api/classify", json={"features": batch_features})
for cls in response.json()["classifications"]:
    print(f"Defect: {cls['defect_type']}, Confidence: {cls['confidence']:.2%}")

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
